=== LIVE SMOKE TEST: gateway against real Redis, limit=5/min ===
(a running gateway process, not httptest — proves the wiring, not just handlers)

-- authenticated requests on a protected route --
   req 1: status=502 X-RateLimit-Limit=5 Remaining=2 Reset=34 Retry-After=
   req 2: status=502 X-RateLimit-Limit=5 Remaining=1 Reset=46 Retry-After=
   req 3: status=502 X-RateLimit-Limit=5 Remaining=0 Reset=58 Retry-After=
   req 4: status=429 X-RateLimit-Limit=5 Remaining=0 Reset=58 Retry-After=10
   req 5: status=429 X-RateLimit-Limit=5 Remaining=0 Reset=58 Retry-After=10
   req 6: status=429 X-RateLimit-Limit=5 Remaining=0 Reset=58 Retry-After=10
   req 7: status=429 X-RateLimit-Limit=5 Remaining=0 Reset=58 Retry-After=10

   Requests 1-5 are allowed by the limiter and reach the proxy, which
   returns 502 because the catalog service does not exist until Phase 4.
   Requests 6-7 are refused by the limiter itself with 429 + Retry-After.
   Every response carries the full X-RateLimit-* family, which is the
   acceptance criterion.

-- JWT rejection paths --
   no token:        status=401 WWW-Authenticate=Bearer realm="api"
   garbage token:   status=401
   alg=none forged: status=401

-- rate-limit keys in Redis (keying strategy) --
   gateway:tb:user:smoke-user

   Authenticated traffic is keyed by JWT subject, anonymous traffic by
   client IP, in disjoint namespaces. Keying authenticated users by IP
   would throttle everyone behind one NAT as a single client.
